claim: RPA tools operate on the user interface of other computer systems in a human-like, outside-in manner, while the underlying information system can remain unchanged.
locator: van der Aalst et al. (2018), Section 1, pp. 269–270.

claim: The 2018 RPA editorial positions RPA in the middle of the long tail of work, between frequent standardized cases and rare cases that remain human-handled.
locator: van der Aalst et al. (2018), Section 2 and Figure 1, pp. 270–271.
notes: The 80/20 language is a Pareto-style motivating illustration, not a universal business law.

claim: A 2023 systematic review selected 32 studies from 605 unique candidate records and found that RPA/process-mining work focuses heavily on UI event capture and preprocessing.
locator: El-Gharib and Amyot (2023), abstract and systematic review findings.

claim: A 2024 RPA selection framework identified 32 criteria; feasibility, process description, and input/output data were among the most-voted criteria, evaluated with 18 processes in six organizations.
locator: Farinha et al. (2024), abstract and process-selection framework.

claim: A 2026 PRISMA-based review synthesizes 83 peer-reviewed journal articles from 2015–2025 into six dimensions and three conceptual pillars; the proposed framework is not empirically validated in that review.
locator: Khantong and Sriboonlue (2026), Abstract, Sections 3–4 and Section 7.

claim: AutoRPA proposes a translator-builder pipeline that distills ReAct-style GUI interaction logic into reusable RPA functions and uses ReAct-based fallback for repair.
locator: Chen et al. (ICML 2026), abstract and method summary.
notes: The paper reports an 82%–96% reduction in token usage on its evaluated similar tasks; this is not a claim of equivalent latency or business ROI improvement.

claim: Wewerka and Reichert's systematic mapping study identified and analyzed 63 RPA publications and derived a framework for comparing RPA research.
locator: Wewerka and Reichert (published online 15 November 2021; Enterprise Information Systems 17(2), 2023), abstract.

claim: A 2026 study expands the corpus to 183 process descriptions and 2,262 labeled activities; synthetic-to-human cross-dataset transfer drops Macro-F1 from 0.935 to 0.648 and automated-class F1 from 0.948 to 0.434.
locator: Chen et al. (2026), abstract, Sections 2.2.2, 3.2.5 and 5.1; published 4 November 2026.

claim: The 2026 BPMNGen study evaluates semantic quality and comprehensibility of LLM-generated BPMN models and reports stronger results on simpler and moderately complex processes than on highly complex ones.
locator: Hörner et al. (2026), abstract and Sections 1 and 7.

claim: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-driven computer-use agents against persistent database ground truth and reports cases where saving a form did not imply correct stored values.
notes: Preprint submitted for review to ICASSP 2027; not a settled industry benchmark standard.

claim: OSWorld contains 369 tasks across real desktop and web applications; its 2024 paper reports 12.24% best-agent task success compared with 72.36% for humans in the reported evaluation.
locator: Xie et al. (NeurIPS 2024), abstract and benchmark results.
notes: These are the 2024 paper's baseline figures, not a 2026 state-of-the-art snapshot.

claim: WindowsWorld (Findings ACL 2026) contains 181 professional tasks across 17 desktop applications, 78% inherently multi-application, and reports under 21% success for leading GUI agents on multi-application tasks.
locator: Li et al. (Findings ACL 2026), abstract and benchmark description.

claim: Stanford AI Index 2026 summarizes a 66.3% OSWorld accuracy result for Claude Opus 4.5, illustrating progress since the original 2024 paper baseline.
locator: Stanford AI Index Report 2026, Chapter 2, Section 2.6 AI Agents, Figure 2.6.2.
notes: Do not compare this value as a clean time series with the original paper's 12.24%; benchmark conditions and model snapshots differ.

claim: If step successes are independent, a sequential workflow's one-shot success probability is the product of its step success probabilities; 0.99^12 is approximately 0.886.
locator: Independent mathematical derivation in the article; no empirical benchmark claim.

claim: With independent transient failure probability q and r retries, the idealized probability of at least one successful attempt is 1-q^(r+1).
locator: Independent mathematical derivation in the article.
notes: Assumes independent failures and no duplicate side effects.

claim: The article derives a simplified break-even case-volume formula from fixed build cost, maintenance cost, manual per-case cost, and automated per-case run cost.
locator: Independent cost-model derivation in the article, Section 12.
notes: Teaching model omits licensing, risk, financing, change-management and error-compensation costs.

claim: The Python invoice workflow is a deterministic teaching simulator demonstrating state transitions, business-rule gates, idempotent writes and read-after-write verification.
locator: Article Section 13 and adjacent rpa_demo.py / test_rpa_demo.py.
notes: FakeERP is not a browser driver or production ERP connector.
